title: Run an x86-64 ISO in Termux with QEMU
voiceover: I wanted to see what a real Linux installer actually does, so I copied an ISO onto my phone to run an x86-64 ISO in Termux. The tutorial's command gave me a black browser tab, an error about SDL, and then a browser that connected to nothing at all. Three separate things were wrong, and not one of them was a QEMU bug.

title: What QEMU on a phone actually is
voiceover: Be honest with yourself about what this is before you start. Termux runs inside Android's app sandbox, so QEMU gets no /dev/kvm , no VT-x and no Hypervisor.framework.

title: Install qemu, and get the package name right
Pick an ISO small enough to be worth it
voiceover: The Alpine releases directory lists three editions of the same distribution, and the size difference is not a rounding error. For x86_64 at the current stable release: virtual is 66 MB, standard is 353 MB, extended is 1 GB .

title: Run an x86-64 ISO in Termux without a graphical app

title: Why -nographic is the wrong flag, and why the port is 5901
voiceover: Most guides tell you to add -nographic . For a text-mode guest that is correct advice.

title: Put the console in the browser (+5 more)
voiceover: A browser cannot speak VNC. VNC is a raw TCP protocol from the 1990s; browsers speak WebSocket and nothing else. title: What to do
voiceover: Install qemu-system-x86-64-headless and qemu-utils . Hyphens in the package, underscores in the command, and check uname -m is aarch64 before you start. Download the Alpine virtual edition, 66 MB, and check it with sha256sum -c before pointing QEMU at it. Run with -accel tcg,thread=multi -display no
bullets: Install qemu-system-x86-64-headless and qemu-utils . Hyphens in the package, underscores in the command, and check uname -m is aarch64 before you start.
Download the Alpine virtual edition, 66 MB, and check it with sha256sum -c before pointing QEMU at it.
Run with -accel tcg,thread=multi -display none -vnc 127.0.0.1:1 . Never -nographic for a graphical ISO, and read the port off QEMU's own output rather than assuming 5900.
Install python-numpy before pip-installing websockify, serve noVNC from the same port as the bridge, and open http://127.0.0.1:6080/vnc.html?autoconnect=1 .
Create a qcow2 inside ~/vms for anything worth keeping, and take the wake lock only for as long as the guest is running.
